life_summary: Richard Roswell Lyman was born in 1870 and came from a prominent LDS family—his father was Francis M. Lyman and his grandfather was Amasa M. Lyman, both apostles. Lyman pursued higher education in engineering, earning a master's degree from the University of Chicago in 1903 and a PhD from Cornell University in 1905. His professional career centered on civil engineering, with significant contributions to road construction and water measurement systems. He received the prestigious J. James R. Croes Gold Medal in 1915 for his engineering work and served as vice-chairman of the Utah State Road Commission and city engineer of Provo. He married Amy Brown in 1896 after eight years of courtship; she later became the eighth Relief Society general president.
church_summary: Lyman was appointed to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1918 and served until 1943. His wife Amy Brown Lyman served as Relief Society general president from 1940 to 1945. In 1943, Church leaders discovered Lyman's long-standing intimate relationship with another woman, and he was excommunicated on November 12, 1943, for violating the law of chastity. At age 83, he was rebaptized on October 27, 1954, though not reinstated as an apostle. When he died on December 31, 1963, his full priesthood blessings were later restored posthumously in 1970.
death_place: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
